summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of Crohn’s disease status post subtotal colectomy was admitted for worsening left lower quadrant abdominal pain and increased diarrhea, concerning for a flare. He reported sudden cessation of bowel movements, prompting ED evaluation. Initial labs showed mild leukocytosis but normal inflammatory markers. MR enterography revealed a 6 cm segment of thickened distal ileum, consistent with chronic Crohn’s, but stable or improved compared to prior studies, with no obstruction. The patient was managed with bowel rest, IV fluids, antibiotics, and pain control. His diet was advanced successfully, and he tolerated oral intake. Stool studies were negative for infection. He reported passive suicidal ideation and concerns about pain management, prompting social work involvement and a care conference. He was discharged home with unchanged medications and plans for outpatient evaluation of bacterial overgrowth.
problems: Adrenal cortical steroids causing adverse effects in therapeutic use
